A. ADMINISTRATIVE ORGANIZATION AND THE 
SHIFTING BALANCE OF CONGRESSIONAL 
AND PRESIDENTIAL POWER
From meager underpinnings in constitutional text, our modern 
administrative authorities, comprising multiple departments, hundreds of 
bureaus, and millions of employees, have gradually emerged. A 2012 
overview of the federal bureaucracy discerned such diversity in the 
organization of and institutional relationships among federal agencies that 
its authors felt compelled to refer to a federal executive “estabhshment,”
